decision_question: Does Maya-XS offer a quality or throughput advantage over ASTRA DeepSeek DSX T16 sufficient to justify keeping its 276.626 GB model weights?

models.profile: ASTRA DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 DSX T16

q172_matched.execution_order: Q173 matched ladder first. Then Maya seeds42/43/44 at131072, followed by DSX T16 seeds42/43/44 at131072, serially; reuse DSX seed42 only if its recorded backend and request fingerprint equal this preregistration, otherwise rerun all three seeds.
q172_matched.backend_parity: Both profiles use Tool-Eval backend label openai and OpenAI wire format. The backend label is not an engine claim; it keeps request construction and report metadata aligned. Q189 historical Maya scores are retained but excluded from the matched mean.

completion.runtime_configuration_caveat: Harness argv requested reasoning_effort=medium for both; DSX request logs reported effort=Some(High). Quality means are descriptive, not a clean comparison under equal effective reasoning settings.

q173_matched.measurement: Run a new Q190 ladder for both models with the same llama-benchy client, official local DeepSeek tokenizer, 262144 server window, 128 exact output tokens, serial C1, no prefix cache, prompt adaptation off, and per-context warmup. At 32K collect three measured samples after one warmup for each model; at 64K/128K/261888 collect one each. Rerun the full DSX ladder: its old ladder used a 1M server window while Maya supports 262144, and is retained as historical only. Target 261888 leaves room for 30 template tokens plus 128 generated tokens within a 262144 window. Effective prefill for Q190 is actual prompt_tokens divided by request-start-to-first-content-token elapsed seconds, derived per request from progress events; llama-benchy raw pp_throughput/est_ppt is diagnostic only when the initial SSE response is empty or role-only.
q173_matched.prefill_metric: Per-request effective prefill TPS = request_end.prompt_tokens / request_first_token.ttft_s. Report the mean of per-request rates per context, plus n and sample SD. This is a conservative end-to-end effective rate and includes small client/network overhead. Do not use benchy pp_throughput when first-response-to-first-content-token is materially delayed; retain that raw field unchanged.

dsx_additional_runs.reason: Reuse historical Q173 32K run and add two repeats to match Maya n=3; other common levels use existing registered T16 n=1.

q173_matched.warmup: Default llama-benchy warmup enabled once per context, matching the historical DSX ladder procedure.

tokenizer.source: pre-existing Q173 pinned tokenizer artifact; no new model/tokenizer download

q173_matched.old_historical_dsx_ladder: Q173 historical 1M-window values remain preserved in Q173/RESULTS.md and the Sheet; excluded from the Q190 matched comparison.

completion.aggregation: equal-weight mean of context-level means for 32K/64K/128K/261888; 32K n=3, others n=1
completion.interpretation: Q173 matched completed: Maya macro P/D 949.10/36.92 tok/s vs DSX 429.14/25.33; Maya was faster on both metrics at all four contexts. Q172 matched also completed; Maya mean 84.67 vs DSX 86.33, with DSX effective reasoning effort logged as High although the harness requested medium. Both failed TC-92 in 3/3 seeds.

safety_gates.unexpected_inference_server: Abort by default. One explicit user-authorized SIGTERM may target only the exact Qwen3.5-9B MTP server on 8021 (amendment-03) or the exact LlamaCode whisper-server on 8081 (amendment-04); preserve the GUI and all unrelated services.
safety_gates.gpu_assignment: same owned model server must be visible on both RTX3090s; preserve Artcraft GUI process

decision_rule.delete_Maya_weights_only_if: matched 3-seed Q172 Maya mean is at least 5 score points below DSX T16; Maya matched-context mean prefill AND decode are both at least 5% lower; and filesystem/reference audit finds no active or PeritoSoft consumer and no unique required capability. Strict dominance required; if mixed/near-tied/uncertain, keep and document why.
decision_rule.if_condition_met: delete only the five exact Maya-XS IQ1_S weight shards and their model-only symlinks after path, size, SHA receipt, open-handle, and consumer checks; preserve Maya runtime, project, Q172/Q173 evidence, sheet history, ASTRA DSX T16, SOL, and shared/unrelated artifacts.
decision_rule.safety: Both models remain eval-only if their matched Q172 reports any TC-92 isolation failure.

observed_outcome.decision: Keep Maya-XS weights. The preregistered deletion gate requires a >=5-point Q172 deficit plus >=5% lower prefill and decode; Maya trails by only 1.67 points and is faster on both Q173 metrics. Keep both profiles eval-only pending a TC-92 fix.

notes: Maya Q189 Q172 at 262144 remains historical and will not be mixed into matched Q172 means.
Q173 8K omitted; context ladder comparison uses only the four common levels.
The lock cleanup archived only a stale completed-task runtime copy; the root lock belongs to this active Q190 task and the historical snapshot lock was preserved.
preregistration_amendment_note: Protocol v4 uses one warmup per Q173 context and derives effective prefill TPS from actual prompt token count / first content-bearing token latency in progress events. The first DSX 32K result was reprocessed from its retained raw trace; remaining measurements use the amended runner. Amendments 03 and 04 authorize one exact-PID SIGTERM only for the identified Qwen3.5 MTP and Whisper servers; no measurement begins until all foreign inference servers are absent and the preflight passes.
